standard_prerequisites.name: The conormal sequence of the diagonal and the identification of the sheaf of differentials with J/J^2
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-differentials-affine (canonical Stacks tag 01UT); the author says at proof lines 903-905 that the diagrammatic set-up is recalled from its proof
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the open W containing the image of the diagonal, the ideal J of the diagonal, the square-zero ideal J^2 and the identification Omega_{X/S} = J/J^2 used throughout.

core_obligations: Set up the first order neighbourhood of the diagonal: choose an open W of X x_S X such that the diagonal induces a closed immersion into W with ideal J, let X' contained in W be the closed subscheme defined by J^2, note that the two projections p_1, p_2 : X' -> X agree after composing with the diagonal, that X -> X' is a closed immersion with square-zero ideal, and that there is a short exact sequence 0 -> J/J^2 -> O_{X'} -> O_X -> 0 with Omega_{X/S} = J/J^2 generated by the local sections p_1^#(f) - p_2^#(f) (proof lines 904-922).

Forward direction: if f is formally unramified then p_1 and p_2 agree on every affine open of X', hence agree everywhere, and the generating description of Omega_{X/S} = J/J^2 gives Omega_{X/S} = 0 (proof lines 924-928).

Converse direction: if Omega_{X/S} = 0 then X' = X; given two morphisms f'_1, f'_2 : T' -> X agreeing on the closed subscheme T defined by a square-zero ideal, the pair defines a morphism T' -> X x_S X whose image lies in W and factors through X' because (f'_1, f'_2)(T) lies in the diagonal; since X' = X the two morphisms agree, which is exactly formal unramifiedness (proof lines 930-940).
proof_roadmap: Recall the diagonal set-up: the open W, the ideal J, the square-zero thickening X contained in X' defined by J^2, and Omega_{X/S} = J/J^2 generated by differences of pullbacks (proof lines 904-922).
Assume f formally unramified, so that the two projections of the first order neighbourhood of the diagonal coincide, and read off the vanishing of Omega_{X/S} (proof lines 924-928).

Conversely assume Omega_{X/S} = 0, so X' = X, and verify the lifting condition for an arbitrary square-zero thickening by producing a morphism to X x_S X and factoring it through the diagonal (proof lines 930-940).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises formal unramifiedness of a morphism f : X -> S by the vanishing of its sheaf of differentials (statement lines 899-900). Both directions are organised around one construction: the first order neighbourhood X' of the diagonal inside X x_S X, cut out by the square of the ideal J of the diagonal, which is a square-zero thickening with Omega_{X/S} = J/J^2 generated by the local sections p_1^#(f) - p_2^#(f) (proof lines 904-922). The forward direction reads formal unramifiedness as p_1 = p_2 and concludes J/J^2 = 0; the converse turns the vanishing into X' = X and then verifies the lifting condition for an arbitrary square-zero thickening by factoring the pair (f'_1, f'_2) through the diagonal, which requires noticing that the image lands in W and that the square-zero condition forces the factorisation (proof lines 930-940). The claim is H2: one construction and two short arguments, no citations beyond the recalled set-up.
